sources.entry: Claude CodePro by Max Ritter - Professional development environment for Claude Code with spec-driven workflow, TDD enforcement, cross-session memory, semantic search, quality hooks, and modular rules integration. A bit "heavyweight" but feature-packed and has wide coverage.

summary.one_liner: QualityLayer (repo maxritter/claude-codepro) is a visual planning and verification environment for coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, with an App, browser, terminal or IDE interface.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a seven-step workflow (Discuss, Research, Plan, Outline, Implement, Verify, Review, Pull request) where plans, decisions and checks are saved as Markdown in the user's repository. Users can comment on mockups, diagrams and clickable artifacts and approve a Plan before code changes. The implementation step is described as test-first, with optional delegation of independent slices. With independent review enabled, a separate agent checks the running change against the request. A code health skill reviews complexity, nesting and duplication. Six installed skills (ql-workflow, ql-artifact, ql-manage, ql-peer, ql-quality, ql-chat) handle planning, artifacts, management, peer sessions, quality and chat. The README does not mention the cross-session memory, semantic search, or quality hooks that the submitted listing description claims; memory appears only as "reuse project lessons" in the App table.
use_cases: plan and review changes before an agent writes code
run a test-first agent workflow with approval gates
get an independent agent review of AI-generated changes
coordinate multiple agent sessions on one machine
how_to_run: Download the QualityLayer App for macOS, Windows or Linux and open it; setup installs the qualitylayer command and connects agents.
curl -fsSL <url> | bash # macOS, Linux, WSL (URL missing from the README text)
irm <url> | iex # Windows PowerShell (URL missing from the README text)
qualitylayer update # if the App does not update itself
qualitylayer uninstall # removes what the installer changed
stack: macOS, Windows and Linux desktop App
notable: Plan and approve changes visually via diagrams and clickable artifacts before code exists
Independent review agent checks the running change against the original request
Each step records decisions and results as Markdown in the repository
Works with several coding agents using the user's own subscription or API key
Skills installed into the agent to route plain-language requests to the right workflow
caveats: Requires a coding agent installed and signed in, plus a paid subscription or API key
The README is marketing-style and names no open-source license; it refers to a LICENSE file without naming it
The listing's claims of cross-session memory, semantic search and quality hooks are not confirmed in the README
Install URLs are missing from the README text supplied
